facts.text: Health care and social assistance, mining, and retail trade are the key sectors of the Timmins economy, accounting for 46% of jobs in the region.
facts.evidence: The key sectors of the economy in Timmins, accounting for 46% of the jobs in the region, are health care and social assistance, mining/quarrying/oil and gas extraction, and retail trade.

facts.text: The Timmins region has 19,195 employed residents, and its economy generates $2.6 billion in household and business incomes.
facts.evidence: The region has 19,195 employed residents, of which 3.3% are immigrants, and the economy generates a total of $2.6 billion in household and business incomes ($62,252 per resident).

facts.text: Timmins is a regional centre for the James Bay basin, providing health, education, culture and business services.
facts.evidence: Timmins ... is a regional centre for the James Bay basin providing services such as health, education, culture and business.

facts.text: The Government of Canada is investing close to $4.2 million to support jobs, growth and the economy in Timmins and surrounding areas.
facts.evidence: Government of Canada invests close to $4.2 million to support jobs, growth and strong economy in Timmins and surrounding areas

meta.fact: a regional centre for the James Bay basin, providing health, education, culture and business services

overview: Timmins had 41,145 residents in 2021, down 1.5% from 41,788 in 2016, living in 17,886 occupied private dwellings across 2,955.33 square kilometres. A stable or slightly shrinking population means growth comes from winning existing customers and from the wider region rather than from newcomers.

Timmins serves as a hub for the James Bay basin, so many customers travel in from surrounding communities for health care, retail and business services. Health care, mining and retail together make up a large share of local jobs.

byService.lead-generation: With the Timmins population down 1.5% since 2016, lead generation should focus on retention, referrals and the regional customers who travel in from smaller northern communities.
byService.seo: Because Timmins draws buyers from across the James Bay basin, SEO should target regional searches as well as Schumacher, South Porcupine and the city's other communities.
byService.website-development: A Timmins website should give out-of-town visitors exactly what they need before a long drive: hours, directions, stock or service details and a way to book ahead.
byService.branding: Branding that respects the city's mining roots and its role as a northern service hub will feel more credible to Timmins customers than generic southern Ontario messaging.
